related_questions.question: What are the four types of COVID vaccines?

text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, there are two primary types of COVID-19 vaccines currently in use: mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) and a protein subunit vaccine (Novavax). The Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) viral vector vaccine is no longer available.
snippet_highlighted_words: mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) and a protein subunit vaccine (Novavax)

list.title: mRNA Vaccines:
list.snippet: These vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) use messenger RNA to instruct cells to produce a harmless piece of the coronavirus spike protein. This triggers an immune response, preparing the body to fight off the actual virus.

list.title: Protein Subunit Vaccine:
list.snippet: The Novavax vaccine contains harmless pieces of the coronavirus spike protein. These proteins are produced in a laboratory and then combined with an adjuvant to enhance the immune response.

list.title: Viral Vector Vaccine:
list.snippet: The Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) vaccine used a modified adenovirus (a common cold virus) to deliver instructions for the spike protein. This vaccine is no longer available in the US, according to the Mayo Clinic.
